prompts: What’s driving customer churn in the Northeast?
How is network performance affecting customer experience?
Where are our biggest revenue opportunities?

churn.title: A service experience gap is driving Northeast churn.
churn.summary: In the dataset, Northeast churn reached 4.8% this quarter, compared with 3.1% nationally. The strongest signal is repeat service disruption among high-value fiber customers.
findings: Customers with two or more network incidents are 2.3× more likely to leave.
Billing-related support contacts increased 18%, creating a second point of friction.
A targeted outreach program for 1,240 at-risk accounts could protect $1.8M in annual revenue.
churn.action: Prioritize proactive service recovery in Boston and New York, then pair it with a targeted loyalty offer.

network.title: Repeat network incidents have the largest experience impact.
network.summary: The network data shows that repeat disruptions, rather than single incidents, correlate most strongly with customer dissatisfaction in the Northeast.
findings: Boston and New York account for 58% of repeat service incidents.
Customers with two or more incidents show a 21-point lower satisfaction score.
Proactive outage notifications are associated with 14% fewer follow-up support contacts.
network.action: Focus remediation on repeat-incident clusters and notify affected customers before they contact support.

revenue.title: Retention and fiber expansion offer the clearest growth path.
revenue.summary: The account and billing data identifies two practical opportunities: protecting high-value accounts and expanding fiber adoption among eligible households.
findings: High-value Northeast accounts with repeat incidents represent $1.8M in annual recurring revenue.
24% of eligible households in the dataset still use legacy broadband plans.
Bundled fiber and wireless accounts have 32% lower churn than single-product accounts.
revenue.action: Start with a service-led retention campaign, then target eligible customers with a fiber and wireless bundle.
